item.title: Lake Biwa's Reed Marshes: Golden Wetlands of the Lakeshore — Guide
item.description: The reed marshes of Lake Biwa are one of the lake’s quietest treasures: broad beds of yoshi reed fringe the shoreline, most beautifully around the Nishinoko lagoon near Omihachiman, where a maze of willow-lined waterways winds between the reeds. These wetlands are a designated cultural landscape, harvested each winter for traditional reed screens and thatch, and alive with herons, grebes and migrating waterfowl. The classic way to experience them is a slow flat-bottomed boat, poled or motored through the corridors of reed that filter the lake’s water and glow gold in the low light of autumn.
